text: TL;DR: The right AI search optimization services depend on your website’s starting condition and on who can implement and measure the work. Check access and indexing first, then business information and content, then outside credibility. Ask any provider for named pages, completed changes, and reports that keep mentions, visits, and inquiries apart. A promised citation count is not evidence. Two proposals can both say “AI search optimization” and describe very different work. One may be a monitoring subscription, another a content program, a third a technical cleanup with a report attached. Without a list of outputs, you cannot tell which one fits your site or whether your current SEO contract already covers part of it. This guide splits the work into six service areas, shows how to pick a starting point, and explains who can carry out each part and how to judge the evidence that comes back. Table of Contents 1 What Are AI Search Optimization Services? 2 Six Services to Match to Your Website's Needs 3 Which Work Should Your Website Prioritize? 4 When Software, In-House Work, or Managed Services Fit 5 What Should Your Reporting Actually Prove? 6 What Changes the Scope and Cost? 7 Frequently Asked Questions 8 Plan the Next Step With TheeDigital What Are AI Search Optimization Services? AI search optimization services are the website, content, business-information, and measurement work that helps a business appear accurately when people use AI-assisted search, such as Google’s AI features, ChatGPT search, Perplexity, and Bing. You will see the same work called generative engine optimization (GEO) or answer engine optimization (AEO). No standard definition covers all three terms. Established SEO still applies. Google’s documentation on AI features and your website treats ordinary SEO foundations as relevant, so a provider who presents SEO and AI search as opposites deserves questions. Using AI tools to research, plan, or produce work is a different matter from improving how your business appears in AI-assisted search, though one engagement can include both. TheeDigital’s AI SEO services cover AI-assisted execution and visibility in AI-generated answers. This guide focuses on the narrower question: whether, and how accurately, your business shows up inside AI answers. No provider is best for every site. The more useful question is which work your website needs first and who will do it. Six Services to Match to Your Website’s Needs The six areas below are an editorial framework, not an industry standard or a fixed package from any provider. Many SEO, content, analytics, and development contracts already include parts of this work. The table turns each label into an output you can ask for and review. Service area Concrete output to request When it matters Baseline and scope A list of buyer questions, the platforms that matter to you, dated observations, and current site performance, with mentions, links, and recommendations recorded separately Before other work starts, so later changes have something to be compared against Technical access and structure A URL-level issue list covering crawling, indexing, snippets, and platform access settings, plus agreed fixes and proof they worked When important pages may be blocked, hidden, or hard to read Content improvement An agreed page list with briefs or revised pages, and named reviewers for factual accuracy When pages leave out what a buyer needs, such as product specifications or service areas Business and entity information Consistent business name, services, locations, and author details across the site and key listings, with markup validated where it applies When different sources describe the same business in different ways Credible third-party presence Named opportunities for editorial coverage, accurate listings, and reputation work, with evidence of what was completed When outside sources say little about your business or describe it wrongly Measurement and conversion review A reporting definition, a change log, and a review that connects visits to inquiries When you cannot tell whether completed work led to anything useful Treat these as suggested scope to request, not as the terms of any provider’s package. Read the last column first. It points to the symptom your own site shows, which is a better starting point than a provider’s list of inclusions. Technical Access and Website Structure Begin with whether the pages that matter can be reached and read. For Google, a page that supports an AI feature needs to be indexed and eligible to appear with a snippet, and Google states that eligibility does not guarantee inclusion. Search Console includes a Search generative AI control . Ask the provider to check the setting on your site and any parent property. Inclusion is the default, so the task is to confirm the current setting matches what you want. Access rules differ by platform. Perplexity, for example, documents a search crawler and notes that a web application firewall may need to allow it. An audit and a list of recommendations can be completed deliverables, yet they do not show that the recommended fixes were implemented. Ask the provider to label each item as a diagnosis, a change made on your site, or a change you must make, and to show a before and after check for the affected URLs. Content and Business Information Google’s guidance for generative AI features points to original, useful content that is clearly organized, and it says no special schema or compulsory chunking is required. In practice, that moves the request away from format tricks and toward facts: what you sell, who it fits, where you work, and what a buyer should do next. Ask for a page list, briefs or revised pages, and a named person who checks technical and factual details. Then ask for consistent business information: the same name, services, locations, and author or company details on your site and in the listings that describe you. Where structured data applies, ask for validation. Markup describes a page. It does not promise a mention. Authority and Measurement Outside credibility covers relevant editorial coverage, accurate listings, and genuine reputation work. Ask for named opportunities and evidence of completed work. Completed placements and published mentions can be inspected as delivery evidence, but they do not establish editorial value, and no provider can guarantee that an AI platform will cite or recommend your business as a result. For measurement, ask for a reporting definition, a change log, and a review that supports decisions, covered in the reporting section below. For platform-level tactics, see how AI search citations work . Which Work Should Your Website Prioritize? Start with the checks that could change everything after them. Confirm that important pages are indexable, readable, and not restricted by a setting nobody remembers changing. If they are restricted, adding content alone does not remove that restriction. Next, read the pages themselves. Do they state what a buyer needs to know? Adding pages does not repair thin ones. If visits already arrive but few turn into useful inquiries, review forms, calls to action, and follow-up before you commission anything aimed at visibility. A missing mention in an AI answer does not tell you which of these applies. Answers vary by platform, wording, location, and account, and one test cannot show why a business is absent. Two hypothetical examples show how the order shifts. Neither is a client account. A manufacturer’s product pages show a model name and a photo, while dimensions, materials, and certifications sit only in downloadable PDFs. Its first move is content improvement: put the missing specifications on the page where a buyer can read them. A local service company with three locations lists different hours and phone numbers on its site and in its listings. Its first move is business information: correct the records so every source describes the company the same way, then decide what new pages are worth writing. Expert Tip: OpenAI’s crawler documentation describes OAI-SearchBot as the crawler for search and GPTBot as the crawler tied to model training, and the two are controlled separately. When a proposal includes robots.txt changes, ask which crawler each rule affects instead of allowing every AI bot at once. A decision about training does not have to match a decision about search access. When Software, In-House Work, or Managed Services Fit The delivery model decides who does the work, so settle it before you settle scope. Software fits when you need observation: tracking sampled prompts, recording mentions and citations, and comparing results over dates. Capabilities vary. Some products only measure, while others help produce or change content, so ask what a given tool actually does. In-house teams fit when someone has site access, editing rights, subject knowledge, and time to make approved changes. Managed services fit when those resources are thin, or when the work crosses technical fixes, content, and outside credibility and needs one coordinator. Many businesses mix them: a tool for observation, internal staff for factual page edits, and an agency for technical and content implementation. Before you add any of it, check your existing SEO, development, and analytics contracts for work you already pay for. Settle who owns accounts, content, and reports. For interview questions and warning signs, see our guide to choosing an AI search optimization agency . What Should Your Reporting Actually Prove? Reports mix different kinds of evidence, and a number from one layer cannot stand in for another. This table shows what each type of evidence can support and where it stops. What you need to know Evidence to review What it cannot establish alone Was the agreed work completed? A change log with affected URLs, dates, and validation results Whether any platform now presents your business differently Does your business appear in sampled AI answers? Dated prompt tests that record mentions, linked citations, and recommendations separately A stable ranking, the cause of a missing mention, or what every user would see What do the platforms report? Impressions in Google’s AI report and citation activity in Bing’s AI report Visits, inquiries, or revenue, and any comparison between the two as if the counts meant the same thing Did visits and actions follow? Session source and medium (where visits came from) plus configured key events (actions marked as important to the business) in Google Analytics Every earlier influence on a visitor; direct traffic or branded search growth should not default to AI credit Did the visits matter to the business? Customer relationship management (CRM) records of qualified inquiries and sales Proof that an AI answer caused a sale, as many buyers cannot be traced back Platform reports cover limited surfaces. Google’s generative AI performance report exposes impressions for its AI features. It does not count prompt-level mentions or conversions. Bing’s AI Performance report shows citation activity on supported surfaces and sampled grounding queries (the phrases used to retrieve content that AI-generated answers reference), and Bing describes Citation Share as an observational measure, not a share of traffic. On your own site, the traffic acquisition report in Google Analytics shows sessions by source and medium and the key events you have configured. It cannot see everything that influenced a visit before it happened. Sampled results change with wording, location, account state, and platform updates. A useful report states the prompts, dates, and method, so one month can be compared with the next. For tool-level detail, read our guide to AI search monitoring . What Changes the Scope and Cost? The same label can cover a small cleanup or a continuing program. These factors move the scope the most: the current condition of the site and its access settings how many priority page types and pages need work the number of locations or product lines how much specialist input the content needs who implements changes and who approves them how deep the reporting goes Ask for an agreed page list and acceptance checks before work starts. A quote with neither is hard to compare with another quote. A one-time cleanup of access and information problems is a different engagement from continuing content, outside presence, and measurement, and a provider should say which one it is pricing. Expert Tip: Google Search Central’s guidance for generative AI features says no special schema is needed to appear in them. If a proposal centers on special AI markup, ask which page information it corrects and how the result will be validated. Structured data can still describe a page accurately, and Google’s statement applies to Google, not to every AI platform. Can my existing SEO provider handle AI search optimization too? Often part of it, as technical access, content, and measurement overlap with SEO. Ask the provider which of the six areas its current scope covers, what it would add, and who implements each change. Capability varies, so check scope instead of assuming. Can I block model training and still allow ChatGPT search discovery? Yes, for OpenAI’s crawlers. Each takes its own robots.txt rule, so you can disallow GPTBot and allow OAI-SearchBot. Allowing search access does not guarantee appearance, and other companies run different crawlers, so check each vendor’s documentation. Does a brand mention matter if there is no link? It can, but a mention is a different signal from a linked citation or a recommendation. It shows your business was named. It does not show a visit, an inquiry, or a sale, so track it apart from clicks and leads. Does AI search optimization require rebuilding my website? Usually not as a starting point. Diagnose access, content, and business information first. A rebuild makes sense when a technical limit, such as pages that cannot be crawled or edited, blocks the agreed fixes. How often should AI search visibility be checked? Choose a documented schedule that fits how often you make decisions and what your team can sustain, and keep the prompts and method the same each time. One run proves nothing about progress, and no frequency is mandatory. text: AI search optimization services help brands achieve visibility in ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google Gemini, Claude, and AI Overviews. As 71.5% of users have tried AI search tools and 14% use them daily, professional optimization has become essential for brands that want to be cited when AI systems generate responses. This guide explains what AI search optimization services include, how agencies approach this work, and how to evaluate providers for your organization. What AI Search Optimization Services Include Professional AI search optimization goes beyond traditional SEO. Agencies offering these services typically deliver a combination of technical implementation, content optimization, and authority building specifically designed for AI citation. LLM Visibility Audits The foundation of AI search optimization is understanding your current visibility. Agencies conduct comprehensive audits that assess: Current citation status: Manual and automated testing across ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, and Google AI Overviews to determine how often your brand appears in AI responses for relevant queries. Share of voice analysis: Comparing your citation frequency against competitors for key topics. Leading agencies like Amsive have developed "LLM Share of Voice" metrics that quantify exactly how often your brand gets cited relative to competitors. Citation accuracy assessment: Evaluating whether AI systems represent your brand correctly when they do mention it. Inaccurate citations can damage brand perception. Content gap identification: Identifying topics where competitors get cited but your brand doesn't, revealing optimization opportunities. Technical AI Optimization AI systems rely on technical signals to understand and trust content. Services in this area include: Schema markup implementation: Adding structured data that makes content machine-readable. FAQ, HowTo, Organization, and Article schema help AI systems understand content structure and intent. Entity optimization: Ensuring your brand, products, and key personnel are clearly defined and consistently represented across all platforms AI systems reference. Passage-level optimization: Structuring content so AI can extract specific sections. LLMs pull from particular passages rather than evaluating entire pages, making content architecture critical. Freshness signal management: Implementing visible timestamps, dateModified schema, and systematic content update schedules. Research shows over 70% of pages cited by ChatGPT were updated within 12 months. Content Optimization for AI Citation Content must be structured specifically for how AI systems retrieve and cite information: Answer-first formatting: Restructuring content so direct answers appear at the beginning of sections before elaboration. Question-format headers: Converting headings into the actual questions users ask AI systems, improving query matching. Modular content architecture: Creating standalone statements AI can extract and cite without losing context. Many agencies apply AEO content guidelines to ensure content is optimized for both traditional search and AI extraction. Citation-worthy data integration: Adding statistics, case study results, and verifiable claims that make content worth referencing. Authority Building Services AI systems evaluate brand authority across the entire web, not just your website. Authority services include: Digital PR campaigns: Securing mentions in authoritative publications that AI systems reference when evaluating credibility. Expert positioning: Building thought leadership through contributed content, interviews, and industry commentary. Review platform optimization: Managing presence on G2, Capterra, and industry-specific review sites that AI systems cite. Cross-platform consistency: Ensuring brand information is identical across LinkedIn, Crunchbase, industry directories, and all platforms AI systems index. For comprehensive evaluation, many organizations start with an AEO audit to identify gaps in cross-platform presence. Ongoing Monitoring and Optimization AI visibility changes constantly. Professional services include: Citation tracking: Regular testing across AI platforms to monitor visibility trends. Competitive monitoring: Tracking when competitors gain or lose AI visibility. Rapid response optimization: Identifying and addressing citation drops quickly. Reporting and analytics: Regular reports showing AI referral traffic, citation frequency, and share of voice changes. How Leading Agencies Approach AI Search Optimization Different agencies take different approaches based on their backgrounds and specializations. Integrated SEO and GEO Approach Some agencies position AI optimization as an extension of traditional SEO. They maintain strong organic rankings while adding layers specifically for AI citation. This approach recognizes that pages ranking in Google's top 10 show approximately 0.65 correlation with LLM mentions. Agencies like Marcel Digital integrate AEO with traditional SEO, arguing the disciplines reinforce each other. Understanding GEO vs AEO differences helps clarify how these optimization approaches work together. PR-Driven Authority Building Other agencies emphasize public relations as the primary lever for AI visibility. Organizations like Chilli Fruit Web Consulting focus on link building, HARO campaigns, media exposure, and editorial placements—building the authority signals AI systems use to evaluate credibility. Case results from PR-driven approaches include achieving 12.5% share of AI search coverage and outranking industry giants in LLM citations. Bottom-Of-Funnel Focus Agencies like Spicy Margarita and Grow and Convert focus on bottom-of-funnel strategies designed to drive revenue rather than traffic. Their GEO approach centers on making brands visible when buyers are actively researching solutions in LLMs. This approach prioritizes commercial queries where AI citations translate directly to qualified leads and demos. Technical and Entity-First Some agencies lead with technical implementation—schema markup, entity optimization, and structured data. They treat content architecture as the foundation that makes other optimizations effective. Skale describes their approach as "passage-level optimization" since LLMs pull from specific sections rather than evaluating entire pages. What Results to Expect Professional AI search optimization delivers measurable outcomes, though timelines vary. Typical Metrics and Timelines 90-day benchmarks: Leading agencies like Maximus Labs report getting clients cited in ChatGPT and Perplexity within 90 days, with measurable increases in AI-sourced demo requests. Citation frequency: Case studies show progression from zero AI visibility to 68% inclusion in AI answers across core queries within approximately 90 days. Lead quality impact: AI-sourced leads often convert at higher rates than organic search—one case study reported 6.2x conversion rate improvement and 290% increase in demo requests. Share of voice gains: Brands achieving double-digit share of AI search coverage after sustained optimization. Realistic Expectations AI search optimization is not instant. Technical implementations can be completed within weeks, but authority building and content optimization require months. Most agencies recommend 3-6 month engagements for meaningful results. AI visibility also fluctuates more than traditional rankings. Positions can change multiple times daily, requiring ongoing monitoring and adjustment. How to Evaluate AI Search Optimization Providers Selecting the right agency requires evaluating several factors. Proven AI-Specific Results Look for case studies demonstrating actual AI citation improvements—not just traditional SEO metrics. Ask for specific examples of clients achieving visibility in ChatGPT, Perplexity, or AI Overviews. Questions to ask: Can you show citation tracking data for previous clients? What share of voice improvements have you achieved? How do you measure AI-sourced leads and conversions? Technical Capabilities Evaluate whether the agency has genuine expertise in AI optimization, not just traditional SEO with new terminology. Questions to ask: How do you approach schema markup for AI optimization specifically? What tools do you use for citation monitoring? How do you handle entity consistency across platforms? Strategic Approach Understand how the agency prioritizes activities and what their theory of influence actually is. Questions to ask: Do you lead with content optimization, PR, or technical implementation? How do you balance traditional SEO with AI optimization? What's your approach to commercial vs. informational queries? Transparency and Reporting AI visibility is harder to measure than traditional rankings. Ensure agencies can demonstrate progress clearly. Questions to ask: How often will you report on AI citation metrics? What does your share of voice reporting look like? How do you track AI referral traffic separately from organic? Investment Considerations AI search optimization services vary significantly in pricing based on scope, agency positioning, and service depth. Most top-tier agencies offer customized pricing based on competitive landscape, number of topics, and existing content foundations. Expect to invest at meaningful levels for comprehensive services. Entry-level programs may start at several thousand dollars monthly, while enterprise engagements with leading agencies can reach significantly higher. The ROI calculation should consider that AI-sourced leads often convert at higher rates than other channels, and early positioning creates compounding advantages as AI search grows. Key Takeaways AI search optimization services help brands achieve visibility when ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other AI systems generate responses. Professional services include LLM audits, technical optimization, content restructuring, authority building, and ongoing monitoring. The core deliverables: Citation audits, schema implementation, content optimization for extraction, digital PR, and continuous monitoring across AI platforms.
